title: Grove has activated its allocation and distribution Primitives while leaving cross-chain and integration Primitives dormant
content:
Reading only the Global Activation Status fields across this chunk gives a compact picture of what Grove actually does today. `Active`: Ecosystem Upkeep Fee, Upkeep Rebate, Distribution Reward (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.1.1.1), Pioneer Chain (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.3.1.1), and the Allocation System Primitive (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.1.1). `Inactive`: Token SkyLink (A.6.1.1.2.2.4.1.1.1), Integration Boost (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.2.1.1), and Light Agent (from A.6.1.1.2.2.2.3.1.1).

The live set clusters on one side of the business: **deploying stablecoin liquidity into yield-bearing positions** (Allocation System) and **rewarding those who bring USDS demand** (Distribution Reward, Pioneer Chain). The dormant set clusters on the other: bridging its own token to other chains (Token SkyLink), subsidizing third-party integrations (Integration Boost), and spawning subordinate Light Agents.

That ordering is consistent with the mandate in A.6.1.1.2.1 — build the credit platform first, because yield generation is the precondition for everything else. Distribution and incentives are only worth paying for once there is a return to distribute.

Because statuses are declared rather than inferred, the Artifact doubles as a **roadmap read backwards**: each `Inactive` Primitive is a capability Grove has provisioned, documented and chosen not to switch on yet. Its own scaffolding tells you which levers exist before any of them are pulled, and a status change is the cheapest possible signal of a strategic shift.
description: Allocation System, Distribution Reward, Pioneer Chain and both upkeep Primitives read Active; Token SkyLink, Integration Boost and Light Agent read Inactive
